title: A Repair Shop's New Service
title_ja: 修理店の新しいサービス
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。人物や出来事は架空の例であり、実在の事業・調査・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A repair shop in an imaginary town has many customers who bring in broken household items.
sentences.ja: 架空の町の修理店には壊れた家庭用品を持ち込む客が多い。

sentences.en: The owner notices that some repairs take only a short time, while other items require more detailed examination.
sentences.ja: 一部の修理は短時間で済むが別の品は詳細検査が必要と店主は気づく。

sentences.en: Customers often visit the shop simply to ask whether an item is worth repairing.
sentences.ja: 客は品が修理する価値があるか尋ねるだけで来店することも多い。

sentences.en: The owner considers introducing a new service that provides information before customers decide what to do.
sentences.ja: 客が判断する前に情報を提供する新サービスを導入しようと考える。

sentences.en: Previously, the shop provided a brief examination without charging customers for that work.
sentences.ja: 以前はその作業に料金を請求せず簡単な検査を提供していた。

sentences.en: However, some examinations require considerable time even when no repair is eventually performed.
sentences.ja: しかし最終的に修理が行われなくてもかなり時間がかかる検査もある。

sentences.en: The owner explains that identifying the cause of a problem can itself be a useful service.
sentences.ja: 問題原因の特定自体が有用なサービスになり得ると店主は説明する。

sentences.en: A customer may avoid an unnecessary purchase after learning more about the condition of an existing item.
sentences.ja: 既存品の状態を詳しく知ることで不要な購入を避けられる客もいるかもしれない。

sentences.en: The shop considers offering an initial assessment at a clearly stated price.
sentences.ja: 店は明示価格で初期評価を提供することを検討する。

sentences.en: Customers would be informed about what the assessment includes and whether further examination might be necessary.
sentences.ja: 評価内容と追加検査が必要になるかもしれないことを客に知らせる。

sentences.en: The owner also considers whether the assessment fee could be included in the price of a subsequent repair.
sentences.ja: 評価料をその後の修理価格に含められるかも検討する。

sentences.en: These arrangements would allow customers to understand the charges before making a decision.
sentences.ja: この仕組みにより客は判断前に料金を理解できるだろう。

sentences.en: The fictional business does not establish a pricing system that would be appropriate for every repair shop.
sentences.ja: 架空事業は全修理店に適した料金制度を確立しない。

sentences.en: Actual businesses would need to examine their costs, customer needs, and the requirements of their services.
sentences.ja: 実事業では費用、顧客ニーズ、サービス要件を調べる必要がある。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the example shows that a useful service does not always produce a physical object or a completed repair.
sentences.ja: それでも有用サービスが常に物理的物体や完了修理を生むわけでないことを示す。

sentences.en: Information can have value when it helps someone make a better decision.
sentences.ja: 情報はよりよい判断を助けると価値を持ち得る。

sentences.en: Customers and businesses need a shared understanding of what is being provided in exchange for money.
sentences.ja: 顧客と企業は金銭と引換に何が提供されるか共通理解が必要だ。

sentences.en: A clear explanation can help distinguish the value of an assessment from the value of the work that may follow.
sentences.ja: 明確な説明は評価の価値とその後の作業の価値を区別する助けになる。

sentences.en: The repair shop's new service illustrates the importance of recognizing work that might otherwise remain invisible.
sentences.ja: 修理店の新サービスはそうでなければ目に見えないままの作業を認識する重要性を示す。

sentences.en: Not every useful result can be held in one's hands.
sentences.ja: 有用な結果すべてを手に持てるわけではない。

vocabulary.definition: using little time or few words
act of obtaining goods for money

questions.prompt: What do customers bring to the shop?
What need motivates the new service?
options: Every broken item requires the same work.
The owner intends to stop repairing things.
Customers want information before deciding about repairs.

questions.prompt: What was previously offered without a fee?
Why can examination have value even without repair?
options: It always produces a new physical item.
It helps customers understand the problem and make decisions.
It guarantees every repair will be performed.
A repair without any information about cost.
A new product unrelated to repairs.
An initial assessment at a stated price.

questions.prompt: Why clarify the charges in advance?
options: Every customer must agree to further work.
The shop wants to hide assessment fees.
Customers can understand what they are paying for before choosing.
questions.explanation_ja: 事前に費用を理解できる。

options: Only the number of household items.
Costs, customer needs and service requirements.
A fictional rule applying to every shop.

questions.prompt: Why mention information as a useful result?
options: Value can exist without a completed physical repair.
Information is always more valuable than every object.
A repair shop should never fix items.
Customers do not need physical goods.
All examinations should be free in every business.
Customers should never ask about prices.
Providing reliable information and assessment can itself be a valuable service.
questions.explanation_ja: 評価と情報提供の価値。

paraphrases.source: However, some examinations require considerable time even when no repair is eventually performed.
paraphrases.rewrite: Inspection may take time despite no repair being done later.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 修理しなくても検査時間はかかる。

paraphrases.source: Customers would be informed about what the assessment includes and whether further examination might be necessary.
paraphrases.rewrite: Customers would learn if additional inspection may be needed.

paraphrases.source: A clear explanation can help distinguish the value of an assessment from the value of the work that may follow.
paraphrases.rewrite: Assessment and any later repair have different kinds of value.
